detailed_findings.finding: Existence of x_r is properly justified from the finite complement property: among infinitely many numbers qm+r, at least one lies in S, so the defining set is nonempty and has a least positive integer.
The proof correctly identifies the gaps in residue class r as exactly r, m+r, ..., (x_r-1)m+r, including the q=0 case via the fact that 0<r<m and m is the least positive element of S.
The step proving all qm+r with q>=x_r lie in S is valid: qm+r = (x_rm+r) + (q-x_r)m, and nonnegative multiples of m belong to S.
The final counting argument via disjoint residue classes modulo m is complete and yields the claimed genus formula.

reason: The proof is correct and complete. It establishes existence of each x_r using finiteness of the complement, shows exactly the first x_r elements in residue class r modulo m are gaps, proves all larger elements in that residue class belong to S by closure under addition with multiples of m, notes there are no gaps in residue class 0, and then counts the disjoint union of gaps across residue classes to obtain genus(S) = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} x_r. This matches the lemma sketch precisely and aligns with the role of translating genus into a linear sum condition.
